title: DIMINUTIVE CEDAR 9 DRAWER KNEE...
reason: Compact nine drawer Victorian pedestal desk catalogued as colonial cedar; useful small size and worth a look at the viewing to confirm the timber, but condition is rough (my guess $100 to $250).
findings: Small Victorian pedestal (kneehole) desk with nine drawers (three across the frieze and three in each pedestal), turned wooden knobs, small brass keyhole escutcheons without keys, moulded top edge with an inset green baize panel that looks modern, and stepped plinth bases. Timber is dark stained; colour fits cedar or mahogany but the species cannot be confirmed from the photos (worn edges show pale wood under the stain). No maker's label, stamp or inscription visible; a hand written tag on the left drawer is illegible. Claimed H-69 L-105 D-52 looks right, so it is smaller than a standard desk.
condition: Distressed: worn dull finish with many small chips and pale edge loss on drawer fronts and the top, scuffed plinths, pale patches on the right side from old labels or tape, baize top replaced and marked. No splits seen but drawer interiors and back not shown.
rescore_note: Small 9 drawer Victorian pedestal desk; the grain is plausibly cedar but unconfirmed and there is no maker mark; rough finish, chips, replaced baize and a low 69 cm height limit appeal, so by the realistic mix of cedar and not it sits at about $150 to $300. Estimate only, no comparable sales checked (search budget used up).
